hints.content:
The function $f$ is positive $($i.e. $f(x)>0)$ whenever its graph is above the $x$-axis.

This is because the positive $y$-values are above the $x$-axis, and $y=f(x)$.



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A coordinate plane. The x-axis scales by one, and the y-axis scales by sixteen. The graph of the function y equals f of x is below the x-axis from x equals negative five to negative four. It is above the x-axis from x equals negative four to negative one. It is below the x-axis from x equals negative one to one. It is above the x-axis from x equals one to four. The function is increasing from left to right unitl x equals negative three. The function decreases from x equals negative three to x equals zero. The function increases indefinitely after x equals zero. The graph is highlighted from x equals negative four to negative one and where x is greater than one.

hints.content: Out of our options, the only correct interval is $-2<x<-1$.
